{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox NCAA team season |mode=Basketball |year=2015–16 |team=Oklahoma Sooners | image = Oklahoma Sooners logo.svg | image_size = 100 |conference=Big 12 Conference |division= |short_conf= Big 12 |CoachRank= 4 |APRank= 7 |record= 29–8 |conf_record= 12–6 |head_coach= [[Lon Kruger]] |hc_year = 5th |asst_coach1= [[Steve Henson]] |asst_coach2= [[Lew Hill (basketball)|Lew Hill]] |asst_coach3= [[Chris Crutchfield]] |stadium=[[Lloyd Noble Center]] |champion= [[Diamond Head Classic]] champions |bowl= [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] |bowl_result = Final Four }} {{2015–16 Big 12 men's basketball standings}} The '''2015–16 Oklahoma Sooners basketball team''' represented the [[University of Oklahoma]] in the [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Sooners were led by [[Lon Kruger]] in his fifth season. They played their home games at the [[Lloyd Noble Center]] in [[Norman, Oklahoma|Norman]], [[Oklahoma]] as a member of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. They finished the season 29–8, 12–6 in Big 12 play to finish in third place. They defeated [[2015–16 Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball team|Iowa State]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2016 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] to advance to the semifinals where they lost to [[2015–16 West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball team|West Virginia]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2016 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated [[2015–16 Cal State Bakersfield Roadrunners men's basketball team|Cal State Bakersfield]], [[2015–16 VCU Rams men's basketball team|VCU]], [[2015–16 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]], and [[2015–16 Oregon Ducks men's basketball team|Oregon]] to be champions of the West Regional and earn a trip to the Final Four for the fifth time in school history. In the Final Four, they lost to the eventual champion [[2015–16 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] by 44 points, the largest margin in Final Four history. ==Previous season== The [[2014–15 Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball team|Sooners]] finished the season 24–11, 12–6 in Big 12 play to finish in a tie for second place. They advanced to the semifinals of the [[2015 Big 12 men's basketball tournament|Big 12 tournament]] where they lost to Iowa State. They received an at-large bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] where they defeated Albany in the second round and Dayton in the third round to advance to the Sweet Sixteen where they lost to Michigan State. ==Departures== {| class="wikitable sortable" border="1" !
